pr.body: Interpolating queries as the initial step. Fixes #107530
pr.title: Query splitting: Interpolate queries at the start of the process

raw_findings.body: applyTemplateVariables() replaces the literal `$__range` text in query.expr before `querySupportsSplitting()`/`isQueryWithRangeVariable()` inspect it, so the check (whose accompanying comment explains it exists precisely to exclude such queries) can no longer find the pattern; the query is now incorrectly split into per-chunk sub-requests, each reusing the already-interpolated full-range value instead of the split sub-range, producing wrong results.
raw_findings.evidence:
const queries = request.targets
    .filter((query) => !query.hide)
    .filter((query) => query.expr)
    .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters));
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent correctness regression: queries with $__range are split and return incorrect time-partitioned data with no error signal.
raw_findings.impact: applyTemplateVariables() replaces the literal `$__range` text in query.expr before `querySupportsSplitting()`/`isQueryWithRangeVariable()` inspect it, so the check (whose accompanying comment explains it exists precisely to exclude such queries) can no longer find the pattern; the query is now incorrectly split into per-chunk sub-requests, each reusing the already-interpolated full-range value instead of the split sub-range, producing wrong results.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` step was inserted ahead of the existing `querySupportsSplitting` partition, changing the order of interpolation vs. the $__range safety check.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable on the original, uninterpolated query.expr, or move the applyTemplateVariables mapping to occur after the querySupportsSplitting partition step.
raw_findings.title: Interpolating query.expr before querySupportsSplitting defeats the $__range split-safety check
raw_findings.trigger: A target's expr contains a range vector using `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` (e.g. `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range])`); templateSrv resolves this built-in variable from the current dashboard time range regardless of scopedVars.

raw_findings.body: applyTemplateVariables() unconditionally calls addAdHocFilters on target.expr; invoking it twice on the same expression can append ad-hoc filter label matchers a second time, producing duplicated/malformed label selectors sent to the Loki backend for sharded requests.
raw_findings.evidence:
const queries = request.targets
    .filter((query) => query.expr)
    .filter((query) => !query.hide)
    .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters));
raw_findings.failure_mode: Sharded split queries can silently contain duplicated ad-hoc filter/label matchers in the generated LogQL.
raw_findings.impact: applyTemplateVariables() unconditionally calls addAdHocFilters on target.expr; invoking it twice on the same expression can append ad-hoc filter label matchers a second time, producing duplicated/malformed label selectors sent to the Loki backend for sharded requests.
raw_findings.root_cause: runSplitQuery unconditionally interpolates request.targets with applyTemplateVariables even when called internally with targets that have already gone through applyTemplateVariables in shardQuerySplitting.ts.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Ensure targets are interpolated exactly once: either have runSplitQuery accept an option to skip re-interpolation for internally-invoked (already-interpolated) targets, or centralize interpolation so shardQuerySplitting no longer double-applies it.
raw_findings.title: Sharded queries are interpolated twice, risking duplicate ad-hoc filters
raw_findings.trigger: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates request.targets via applyTemplateVariables, then splitQueriesByStreamShard()'s runNextRequest() builds subRequest.targets from these already-interpolated targets (plus shard-label additions) and calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...), which itself independently re-runs `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` on the same targets.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test asserting a query with `[$__range]` in its expr is still routed as a single non-split request (querySupportsSplitting returns false) after the interpolation reordering.

finding.verifier_reason: Patch line R299 adds `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` before line R300's `partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query))`. The `querySupportsSplitting` function at L282-288 explicitly checks `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to exclude queries containing `$__range`. Since `applyTemplateVariables` replaces template variables including `$__range` before this check runs, the literal `$__range` pattern will no longer be present in `query.expr`, defeating the safety check. This is a concrete ordering bug introduced by the patch.

finding.title: Sharded queries are interpolated twice, risking duplicate ad-hoc filters
finding.trigger: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates request.targets via applyTemplateVariables, then splitQueriesByStreamShard()'s runNextRequest() builds subRequest.targets from these already-interpolated targets (plus shard-label additions) and calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...), which itself independently re-runs `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` on the same targets.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that sharded queries are interpolated twice is incorrect. The patch shows `runShardSplitQuery` at L48-52 calls `applyTemplateVariables` once on `request.targets`. When `runSplitQuery` is called at L163, it receives `subRequest` with targets from `interpolateShardingSelector(targets, shardsToQuery)` at L154, where `targets` came from `adjustTargetsFromResponseState(groups[group].targets, ...)` at L146. The `groups[group].targets` are the already-interpolated `splittingTargets` passed to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. However, `runSplitQuery` at R296-299 will call `applyTemplateVariables` again on these already-interpolated targets. This is a valid concern, but the candidate incorrectly claims ad-hoc filters are the issue - `applyTemplateVariables` does call `addAdHocFilters`, but the patch context doesn't prove this causes duplicate filters since the first interpolation in `runShardSplitQuery` also uses `applyTemplateVariables`. The double-interpolation is real but the specific ad-hoc filter duplication claim is unverified.
